short: The printed or digital proof of a completed sale.
seoTitle: Receipt — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: A receipt is the document given to a customer as proof of a completed sale, showing items, amounts, tax and payment mode.
definition: A receipt is the document given to a customer as proof of a completed sale, showing items, amounts, tax and payment mode. It may double as the tax invoice where the prescribed particulars are included.
bodyHtml:
Why Receipt matters

Receipts are the customer's record and often the business's only proof of what was sold at what price. For returns and warranty claims, the receipt is the entire evidence.

How Receipt works in practice

Include everything a tax invoice needs when serving business customers, and keep a digital copy regardless. A QR code for payment or reviews on the receipt costs nothing and gets read.

faq.question: Is a receipt the same as a tax invoice?
faq.answer: Only if it carries all the prescribed particulars. A simple payment acknowledgement is not a tax invoice.

faq.question: Should I offer digital receipts?
faq.answer: They cost nothing to send, cannot fade, and give you a customer contact for later.
